title: Score Mixture Design Model(s)
modelselector1: Click one or more mixture models created by Analyze Mixture Design -- all selected models must share the same mixture components
labelModelResponseValues:
Mixture components used by the selected model,
in the order Analyze Mixture Design recorded them
totalAmount: Total amount the model's components should sum to (same units used when the model was fit)
sumTolerance: Sum tolerance (optional -- leave blank to use 0.5% of Total)
lblMixtureCheckNote: Every row's selected mixture components are checked against Total before scoring. Unlike a generic prediction/scoring tool, this dialog does not silently extrapolate a mixture model to rows where the components don't actually sum to Total -- that would evaluate the model far outside the constrained region it was ever validly fit on.
predictAnywayChk: Still predict for rows outside the mixture region (NOT recommended -- produces extrapolated, statistically invalid predictions)
showFlagColumnChk: Add a column flagging which rows were inside vs. outside the mixture region
prefixInput: Column name prefix (optional -- leave blank to use each model's own response name)
showConfidenceIntervalChk: Save confidence interval (uncertainty in the mean response)
showPredictionIntervalChk: Save prediction interval (uncertainty for a new single observation -- wider)
level: Confidence level (applies to whichever interval(s) are checked above)

help.title: Score Mixture Design Model(s)
help.body:
Description
Scores the active dataset using one or more mixture models created by Analyze Mixture Design, adding predicted response columns -- and optionally confidence or prediction intervals -- for each selected model.

Why this dialog exists instead of the general-purpose Model Scoring dialog
The general Model Scoring dialog only checks that a model's required predictor columns exist in the dataset being scored -- it never checks that their values actually sum to the mixture's Total. A row where the selected components sum to, say, 120 instead of 100 would still get a prediction from that dialog, silently extrapolating the model far outside the constrained simplex it was ever fit on. This dialog checks that explicitly, row by row, before trusting any prediction.

Selecting models
Only select models created by Analyze Mixture Design (these carry the component-name metadata this dialog checks automatically). All selected models must share the identical set of mixture components, and must be fully estimated (no rank-deficient/NA coefficients) -- this dialog validates both before scoring anything.

Rows outside the mixture region
By default, any row whose selected components do not sum to Total (within the specified tolerance) is left with a missing (NA) prediction rather than a silently-extrapolated value. Check "Still predict for rows outside the mixture region" only if you specifically understand and want that extrapolation.

Confidence vs. Prediction intervals
A confidence interval describes uncertainty in the average response at a given blend; a prediction interval describes uncertainty for one new individual measurement at that blend, and is always wider. Both are valid for the no-intercept Scheffé models this dialog scores, since predict.lm() is fully formula-driven and treats a mixture model's interaction/three-way terms no differently from an ordinary regression's.
